messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Population names - how to completely change
messages.subject_clean: [dartR] Population names - how to completely change
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I had a bit of trouble with this, assigning populations to an exon capture dataset read in as a fasta.

What worked was:
gl <- fasta2genlight("snp_align_one_snp_gene_r_0.fasta")
#read in csv file with population names
pops <- read.csv("pop_reassign.csv")
pops$pop <- as.factor(pops$pop)
#assign populations
gl@other$ind.metrics$sites <- pops$pop
gl@pop <- gl@other$ind.metrics$sites

The key thing was getting the pops file perfectly formatted. I compared it to an existing dataset with automated assignments.

Renee

messages.subject: genotype likelihoods from DART data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi DART-ers,

Has anyone calculated genotype likelihoods from DART data?
This would be similar to the "GL" data in VCF format?
Specifically, metadata listed here for GL: https://faculty.washington.edu/browning/intro-to-vcf.html

I have gone through the DART metadata file and the information to calculate this should be available but not sure if it is already built into the DARTr package?

Thanks in advance!
cheers,
Kate

messages.subject: Re: genotype likelihoods from DART data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kate,

The calculation of genotype likelihoods are not yet implemented in the pipeline of DArT and some information required to calculate the likelihoods (e.g. read quality) is only provided by DArT if requested. However, I talked with DArT's bioinformaticians and we agreed that is an important issue worth exploring. If you like we could use your dataset as a case study to implement genotype likelihoods in DArT and dartR. If you agree just send me your DArT service number in a private e-mail.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: gl2gds and gl2plink is not working when i added chromosome and its position; while its working well without it.
messages.subject_clean: gl2gds and gl2plink is not working when i added chromosome and its position; while its working well without it.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajneesh,

It seems that the function requires that loci are ordered by position. Can you try the following code.

# ordering loci by position
> gl5 <- gl5[,order(gl5$position)]
# ordering loc.metrics by position
> gl5$other$loc.metrics <- gl5$other$loc.metrics[order(gl5$other$loc.metrics$Position),]
# run the function with the ordered dataset

> gl2gds(gl5, outfile="Ayb_callR0.80_Repavg_95_maf_0.01_miss20%_2.5KSNP.gds", outpath = ".")

Please let us know if it worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis

Please let us know whether it worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nikki,

Thank you for your kind words :)

1) In this case gl.recalc.metric is used to calculate metrics for each locus that are not calculated by default in other programs and are required for various functions in dartR. Actually, the main difference that I suggested is:

Fourpop.gl_2$other$loc.metrics <- as.data.frame(Fourpop.gl_2$other$loc.metrics)

I suggested this because the function gi2gl formats the slot "loc.metrics" as a list when it should be a data frame. We will fix this soon and should be available in the next release of dartR, however in case you want to have the latest version of the package you can download the developer version via:
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")

2) You can try:

x <- yourdata.gl <http://yourdata.gl>
na.counter <- 0
loc.list <- array(NA, nLoc(x))
  mat <- as.matrix(x)
  lN <- locNames(x)
  for (i in 1:nLoc(x)) {
    row <- mat[, i]
    if (all(row == 0, na.rm = TRUE) | all(row == 2, na.rm = TRUE) |
        all(is.na <http://is.na>(row))) {
      loc.list[i] <- lN[i]
      if (all(is.na <http://is.na>(row))) {
        na.counter = na.counter + 1
      }
    }
  }
  loc.list <- loc.list[!is.na <http://is.na>(loc.list)]

# display list of monomorphic loci

  print(loc.list)

# NB We will add an option to this function to make more accessible the off monomorphic loci

3) The correction for multiple tests used in the HWE function is the "standard" Bonferroni correction method not the sequential Bonferroni correction a.k.a. Holm-Bonferroni. The "standard" Bonferroni method is more stringent than the Holm-Bonferroni.

Cheers,

Luis
